title: Generators that feed each other
description:
Generators compose: one can consume another, and nothing is computed until the final loop asks for it.

Write three:

- `std::generator<int> naturals(int from)`: `from`, `from + 1`, ... for ever.
- `std::generator<int> primes()`: every prime number in order, for ever. Loop over `naturals(2)` and `co_yield` the ones that are prime.
- `std::generator<std::string> words(std::string text)`: the words of a text one at a time, splitting on spaces (runs of several spaces count as one separator; no empty words).

`words` takes its text **by value** on purpose. A coroutine keeps its parameters alive while it is paused; a reference or `std::string_view` to something of the caller's could dangle by the time the coroutine resumes.
hints: `naturals` is an endless loop yielding `from++`. `primes` does `for (int n : naturals(2)) if (isPrime(n)) co_yield n;`.
For `words`, walk the text, skip runs of spaces, find the end of each word and `co_yield` it as a `std::string`.
